facts.fact: The article says there are millions of apps in the App Store and Google Play, which makes discovery a major challenge (the author's general claim, not a sourced figure).

facts.fact: Google App Campaigns let an advertiser set a target cost per install, and Google's machine learning then optimizes delivery across Search, Display, YouTube, and Google Play.
facts.quote: You set your target cost per install and let Google's machine learning optimize delivery.

facts.fact: Apple Search Ads place an app's ad at the top of App Store search results when users search for terms like 'expense tracker', and the article recommends starting with Search Match to find download-driving queries.
facts.quote: Start with Search Match to discover which queries drive downloads

facts.fact: The article states that a creator with 20,000 engaged followers in a niche typically generates more installs per dollar than one with millions of general followers (an illustrative claim with no source).
facts.quote: A creator with 20,000 engaged followers in your niche typically generates more installs per dollar than one with millions of general followers.

facts.fact: The article cites Dropbox as a company that grew through referrals by offering free storage space to referrers and new users.
facts.quote: Dropbox famously grew through referrals by offering free storage space.

facts.fact: Gaming apps might see $1-3 CPIs on some networks, according to the page.
facts.quote: Gaming apps might see $1-3 CPIs on some networks while B2B productivity apps might pay $5-15 or more.

facts.fact: The page gives an example of an app with a $2 cost per install but a $20 cost per action for paying users.
facts.quote: An app might have a $2 CPI but a $20 CPA for paying users.

facts.fact: The page gives an example of a user who generates $50 in lifetime revenue, for whom significantly more acquisition spend is affordable than for a user generating $5.
facts.quote: If a user generates $50 in revenue over their lifetime, you can afford to spend significantly more than if they generate $5.

facts.fact: The page suggests starting user acquisition with roughly $500-1,000 spread across a few channels.
facts.quote: Even $500-1,000 across a few channels will teach you which messages resonate and which audiences convert.

facts.fact: The page gives an example of an install costing $3 that generates $15 in lifetime value.
facts.quote: If an install costs $3 and generates $15 in lifetime value, you can calculate exactly how much to invest.
